# Code base map

One line per module, taken from its `!@descr:` header; directory
descriptions come from `<dir>/<dir>.inf`. Regenerate with
`python3 scripts/generate_codeoverview.py`.

- **src/** — the sources of the library and of its test executable: defs/ (shared constants and vocabularies), core/ (the hand-written Fortran layer), test/ (test-only code)
  - **core/** — the hand-written Fortran layer: mlxf with the capability folders runtime/, array/, ops/, linalg/, fft/, compile/, transforms/, random/, fast/, io/ and distributed/
    - **array/** — the mlx_array type (lifetime, evaluation, operators, closure vectors), the data movement of mlxf_transfer, and mlxf_calls, the signature helpers several families share
      - `mlxf_array.f90` — the mlx_array type: its interface; lifetime, evaluation, operators and closure vectors in submodules
      - `mlxf_array_closure.f90` — checked conversion between C closure vectors and owned Fortran arrays
      - `mlxf_array_elementwise.f90` — the operators of mlx_array: arithmetic, powers, comparisons, boolean operators, unary signs, and exp
      - `mlxf_array_evaluation.f90` — evaluation and what it settles: mlx_eval, mlx_async_eval, mlx_synchronize, the sizes of an array and of its buffer
      - `mlxf_array_lifetime.f90` — the lifetime of an mlx_array: the defined assignment, release, kill, finalization, adoption, the handle check, the getters
      - `mlxf_array_tester.f90` — tests of mlxf_array: the leak gate, byte identity of data movement, memory order, views, the zero-copy table
      - `mlxf_calls.f90` — the shared signature helpers: the calls of mlx-c several families make, and the checks they share
      - `mlxf_calls_checks.f90` — the checks and translations the helpers share: dtypes, dimensions, sections, positions, streams
      - `mlxf_calls_elementwise.f90` — the unary and binary signature classes and weak scalars, the helpers the operators share
      - `mlxf_calls_shaped.f90` — the signature helpers several operation families share: an option, a dtype, a shape, axes, lists
      - `mlxf_transfer.f90` — data movement between Fortran arrays and mlx_arrays: copies, scalars, read-only views and writable buffers
      - `mlxf_transfer_borrow.f90` — shared storage: mlx_view (read-only borrowing after evaluation) and mlx_alloc (writable initialisation of page-aligned memory)
      - `mlxf_transfer_copy.f90` — copies between Fortran arrays and mlx_arrays: mlx_from, mlx_to, mlx_to_alloc, mlx_item
    - **compile/** — Fortran closures and graph compilation with checked callback boundaries
      - `mlxf_compile.f90` — owned Fortran callbacks as MLX closures and compiled functions
      - `mlxf_compile_tester.f90` — Fortran callbacks, byte-exact compiled results, shapeless reuse and callback error recovery
      - `mlxf_export.f90` — functions written to a file and read back: one trace or several, and the imported function as a counted handle
      - `mlxf_export_tester.f90` — exported and imported functions, one trace and several, and the compilation controls, against the callback's own results
    - **distributed/** — distributed groups and collectives, tested on the group of one process
      - `mlxf_distributed.f90` — distributed computing: a group of processes behind a counted handle, and the collectives and messages between its members
      - `mlxf_distributed_calls.f90` — signature-class helpers of the distributed operations: an array or a shape, a peer, a group that may be absent
      - `mlxf_distributed_tester.f90` — distributed groups and collectives on the group of one process, and, by name only, a ring of two processes
    - **fast/** — fast: fused layers (normalisations, rotary embeddings, attention, cross entropy) and custom Metal kernels behind a counted handle, and their tests
      - `mlxf_fast.f90` — MLX's fast module: fused layers along dimension 1, and custom Metal kernels behind a counted handle, applied on the GPU
      - `mlxf_fast_calls.f90` — signature-class helpers of the fused layers: normalisations with optional weights, rotary embeddings, attention
      - `mlxf_fast_layers_tester.f90` — the fused layers against plain Fortran loops: layer and RMS normalisation, cross entropy, rotary embeddings, attention
      - `mlxf_fast_tester.f90` — custom Metal kernels against exact Fortran references: buffer layout, several buffers, templates, atomics, compiled use, refusals
    - **fft/** — fft operations and their two-device tests
      - `mlxf_fft.f90` — real and complex Fourier transforms along Fortran dimensions, their shifts and their frequencies
      - `mlxf_fft_nd_tester.f90` — transforms over several dimensions, the real ones' half-size dimension, the shifts and the frequencies against direct double-precision transforms
      - `mlxf_fft_tester.f90` — independent two-device checks of fft values and Fortran conventions
    - **io/** — arrays in files (npy, safetensors, GGUF), the text of a graph, and their round-trip tests
      - `mlxf_io.f90` — arrays in files: NumPy's .npy, safetensors and GGUF, and the text of a graph
      - `mlxf_io_calls.f90` — helpers of file input: an array read on the CPU's stream, and the arrays of a map or of a GGUF file as counted handles
      - `mlxf_io_tester.f90` — arrays in files: byte-identical .npy round trips of every transfer kind and rank, the header's reversed shape, safetensors, GGUF, graph text, sizes
    - **linalg/** — products, matrices in the Fortran view (factorisations, solvers, norms), convolutions, and their two-device tests
      - `mlxf_conv.f90` — convolutions with Fortran dimensions: channels first, then the spatial dimensions, the batch last
      - `mlxf_conv_tester.f90` — the convolutions and transposed convolutions over one to three spatial dimensions against direct real64 sums in Fortran's layout
      - `mlxf_linalg.f90` — products with Fortran dimensions: matrix products (batched, gathered, masked, segmented, added), inner, outer, Kronecker and cross products, contractions and Einstein sums
      - `mlxf_linalg_matrix.f90` — matrices in the Fortran view: factorisations, inverses, determinants, eigenvalues, solvers and norms
      - `mlxf_linalg_matrix_tester.f90` — the factorisations, inverses, determinants, eigenvalues, solvers and norms by residuals, orthogonality and constructed spectra
      - `mlxf_linalg_mm_tester.f90` — the gathered, block-masked and segmented matrix products against Fortran's matmul on the selected blocks
      - `mlxf_linalg_products_tester.f90` — the inner, outer, Kronecker, dot and cross products, contractions, Einstein sums, the added matrix product and the Hadamard transform against plain Fortran loops
      - `mlxf_linalg_tester.f90` — independent two-device checks of linalg values and Fortran conventions
    - **ops/** — the operations in Fortran conventions, one module per concern (elementwise, math, logic, shape, index, reduce, create, sort), and their two-device tests
      - `mlxf_ops_create.f90` — constructors: ones, fills, arrays shaped like another, identity and triangular matrices, grids and windows
      - `mlxf_ops_create_tester.f90` — table-driven two-device checks of the constructors: ones, fills, the *_like family, matrices, grids, windows
      - `mlxf_ops_elementwise.f90` — elementwise operations through the array signature helpers
      - `mlxf_ops_index.f90` — gathers, scatters, section updates, searches and unique values through the array signature helpers
      - `mlxf_ops_index_tester.f90` — two-device checks of gathers, scatters, section updates, searches and unique values against Fortran loops
      - `mlxf_ops_logic.f90` — predicates, closeness and equality tests, and the integer and bitwise functions
      - `mlxf_ops_logic_tester.f90` — table-driven two-device checks of the predicates, closeness and equality tests and the integer and bitwise functions
      - `mlxf_ops_math.f90` — elementwise arithmetic and transcendental functions, rounding, clipping and NaN replacement
      - `mlxf_ops_math_tester.f90` — table-driven two-device checks of the elementwise arithmetic and transcendental functions
      - `mlxf_ops_reduce.f90` — reductions, scans, softmax and extremum positions through the array signature helpers
      - `mlxf_ops_reduce_tester.f90` — table-driven two-device checks of the reductions, scans, softmax and extremum positions
      - `mlxf_ops_shape.f90` — shape operations through the array signature helpers
      - `mlxf_ops_shape_calls.f90` — the signature helpers of the shape operations: one per C signature class of mlx-c's shape functions
      - `mlxf_ops_shape_tester.f90` — two-device checks of the shape operations against Fortran's own array expressions
      - `mlxf_ops_sort.f90` — sorting, partitioning and the largest elements through the array signature helpers
      - `mlxf_ops_sort_tester.f90` — two-device checks of sorting, partitioning and the largest elements against plain Fortran sorts
      - `mlxf_ops_tester.f90` — independent two-device checks of ops values and Fortran conventions
    - **random/** — random keys and samplers in Fortran shapes, and their two-device tests
      - `mlxf_random.f90` — random keys and samplers: samples in Fortran shapes, parameters that broadcast, one-based categories and permutations
      - `mlxf_random_calls.f90` — signature-class helpers of the samplers: a Fortran shape, operands, an optional key, the default or the CPU stream
      - `mlxf_random_tester.f90` — the random keys and samplers: keys and determinism, Fortran shapes, moments of every sampler, one-based categories and permutations
    - **runtime/** — the runtime the array type stands on: libc entry points, errors, the handle registry, devices, memory, versions
      - `mlxf_device.f90` — devices and initialisation: the backend, the device count, the default device, device information, the default stream
      - `mlxf_device_tester.f90` — tests of mlxf_device: the backend, device counts, the default device, device information
      - `mlxf_error.f90` — errors: the mlx-c error handler, the hard-error stop, checked statuses, the last error and the one-thread guard
      - `mlxf_error_tester.f90` — tests of mlxf_error: recorded messages, checked statuses, and recovery from a failed evaluation
      - `mlxf_libc.f90` — the C library entry points the library calls (strlen, memcpy, posix_memalign, free, fopen, fclose, dup, fdopen) and C-string copies
      - `mlxf_memory.f90` — MLX's memory controls: active, peak and cache memory, the cache and memory limits
      - `mlxf_memory_tester.f90` — tests of mlxf_memory: active, peak and cache memory follow an array's life; the limits are set and restored
      - `mlxf_registry.f90` — the handle registry: each live MLX object (its ctx address) with a serial and a Fortran-side reference count
      - `mlxf_registry_tester.f90` — tests of mlxf_registry: reference counts, serials, the diagnosis of copies made without the defined assignment
      - `mlxf_stream.f90` — streams: a device's queue of work behind a counted handle, the default stream of a device, and waiting for one
      - `mlxf_stream_tester.f90` — streams and the runtime controls added with them: device availability, the memory and wired limits, Metal capture
      - `mlxf_version.f90` — versions of mlx-fortran, of the mlx-c it was built against and of the MLX it runs on; the runtime description
      - `mlxf_version_tester.f90` — tests of mlxf_version: the toolchain links mlx-c and the MLX it loads is one mlx-c 0.8 supports
    - **transforms/** — function transforms (gradients, vjp, jvp, custom rules) against closed-form derivatives on both devices
      - `mlxf_transforms.f90` — function transforms: values and gradients, vector-Jacobian and Jacobian-vector products, custom derivatives, checkpoints
      - `mlxf_transforms_tester.f90` — the function transforms against closed-form derivatives: gradients, vector-Jacobian and Jacobian-vector products, custom rules
    - `mlxf.f90` — the user module of mlx-fortran: re-exports the public names of the mlxf_* modules
  - **defs/** — the constants and vocabularies shared by more than one module of mlx-fortran (exported = defs, local = stay)
    - `mlxf_defs.f90` — the constants and vocabularies more than one module uses: the hard-error status, the devices, the dtypes
  - **test/** — test-only code compiled into mlxf_test_exec: framework/ (assertions, the suite registry, the ABI probe), toys/ (the toys that mirror SIMPLE, one folder per toy), oracles/ (their independent references), bench/ (the benchmarks)
    - **bench/** — the benchmarks run by hand (mlxf_test_exec test=bench_<x>): the polar table, the projector, the reconstruction and the insertion probe
      - `mlxf_bench_blas.f90` — the crossover of BLAS and MLX matrix products: sgemm and cgemm on the host against matmul on MLX's devices
      - `mlxf_bench_insert_probe.f90` — the protected-update probe: SIMPLE's gridding insertion as one Metal kernel with atomic float32 deposits, against the oracle
      - `mlxf_bench_polar_table.f90` — benchmark of the polar table workspace at SIMPLE's sizes: accuracy block, timing sweep, profile, overlap, shift maps
      - `mlxf_bench_projector.f90` — benchmark of the toy projector at SIMPLE's sizes: the reprojection of one state timed, chained to family A, and judged
      - `mlxf_bench_recon_pcg.f90` — benchmark of the toy reconstructor_pcg at SIMPLE's boxes: transforms, timing, profile, probe, accuracy
    - **framework/** — the test library: assertions and the summary, the suite registry, the test definitions, the NaN-safe reductions, and the ABI probe of the generated layer (a C header, its echo functions compiled by Apple's clang, and the tester)
      - `mlxf_abi_tester.f90` — the ABI probe: every argument and result class of the generated bind(c) layer echoed by C, and the C layouts
      - `mlxf_test_defs.f90` — what test modules share: the polar pipeline's constants, tunables, tolerances and behaviourless records
      - `mlxf_test_reduce.f90` — NaN-safe maximum for test code: a NaN anywhere makes the result +infinity, so no tolerance accepts it
      - `mlxf_test_registry.f90` — the area suites and guard groups of mlxf_test_exec: sub-suites per area, and the members of each guard group
      - `mlxf_test_utils.f90` — assertions, suite tracking and the summary of mlxf_test_exec
    - **oracles/** — independent double-precision references the toys and the benchmarks are judged against: DFTs, polar scores and shift maps, poses, projections, gridding, the reconstruction's fixture and PCG, with their self-checks
      - `mlxf_oracle_dft.f90` — host oracle: direct discrete Fourier transforms in complex double precision, 1D and 3D, and their self-check
      - `mlxf_oracle_gridding.f90` — host oracle of the gridding insertion on the native grid: accumulators, stored half, density correction, map
      - `mlxf_oracle_pcg.f90` — host oracle of the PCG problem: stencil matrix, transform operator, preconditioner, Cholesky and PCG solves
      - `mlxf_oracle_polar.f90` — the polar fixtures' shared tools: ring DFT, keyed variates, the memo-level oracle, checks of rows and draws
      - `mlxf_oracle_polar_objfun.f90` — host oracle of the polar objectives: Euclidean loss, two correlations, in-plane and reference reductions
      - `mlxf_oracle_polar_shiftmap.f90` — host oracle of the polar shift map: grid, cell, truncated Bessel form, areas, mode and width
      - `mlxf_oracle_pose.f90` — host oracle of the pose objective: prepared reference, quadratic B-spline gather, objectives, derivatives, solve
      - `mlxf_oracle_projection.f90` — host oracle of the Fourier projection and its adjoint: window, explicit matrix, gather, scatter, packed half
      - `mlxf_oracle_projection_tester.f90` — tests of the projection's host oracles: the self-checks of the direct transforms and of the projection asserted
      - `mlxf_oracle_recon_fixture.f90` — the full-coverage fixture of the reconstruction's PCG solve: planes on a golden-angle spiral, two blobs, packed accumulators
      - `mlxf_oracle_recon_pcg.f90` — host oracle of the reconstruction as its conjugate-gradient solver sees it: lattice, kernel, operator, solve
    - **toys/** — the toys that mirror SIMPLE's classes: the opaque device state they hold, the seam tester, and one folder per toy (polar, projector, recon)
      - **polar/** — the polar toy: polarft_calc with its GPU workspace, the table driver eul_prob_tab, the fixture of the polar host route, and their testers
        - `mlxf_polarft_host_fixture.f90` — the fixture of the polar host route: seeded rings, a table filled through the toy driver on either backend, the table's lines
        - `mlxf_toy_eul_prob_tab.f90` — the toy table driver (test only): a miniature of SIMPLE's eul_prob_tab that fills the dense table through the polar calculator
        - `mlxf_toy_eul_prob_tab_tester.f90` — tests of the toy table driver: the fill's order, blocks and keyed draws, the two coarse maps set up by SIMPLE's rule, refusals
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_block.f90` — the toy polar calculator's block scoring: score_block_posterior with SIMPLE's block kernel, and the blocks in flight
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_block_mlx.f90` — the toy polar calculator's block scoring on MLX (glue): a block queued in its parity's workspace and collected from it
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_calc.f90` — the toy polar calculator (test only): a miniature of SIMPLE's polarft_calc with its device state as one opaque component
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_calc_tester.f90` — tests of the toy polar calculator's dense route: the fixture, the ring oracle, the draw, the contract, schedule identity, the tail's forms
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_core.f90` — the toy polar calculator's core: new, kill, the particles' halves, the shell weights, the tile plan and tail, the message
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_core_mlx.f90` — the toy polar calculator's core on MLX (glue): the device state of a new calculator, the device route's projected bank
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_host_tester.f90` — tests of the polar toy's host route: SIMPLE's block kernel against the ring oracle, the team's table, the fill's two branches
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_memo.f90` — the toy polar calculator's memoization: the setters' staging, the ring transforms of references and particles, the reference tiles
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_memo_mlx.f90` — the toy polar calculator's memoization on MLX (glue): the device route's sections and memos, the resident reference tiles
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_shiftmap.f90` — the toy polar calculator's shift maps: new_shiftmap, setup_shiftmaps, gen_shiftmap, shiftmap_mode and their inquiries
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_shiftmap_mlx.f90` — the toy polar calculator's shift maps on MLX (glue): a map's resident data on both parities, the maps of a block, the inquiries
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_shiftmap_tester.f90` — tests of the toy polar calculator's shift maps: analytic ring fixtures, the direct residual oracle, mode, width, evidence
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_tail_tester.f90` — tests of the polar calculator's fused tail: the refusal on the CPU device, the two kernels' identity, repeatability, small tiles, objects
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_workspace.f90` — the polar calculator's GPU workspace (test only): one parity's resident reference tiles, the entries' graph, the shift maps
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_workspace_lifecycle.f90` — the polar workspace's lifecycle: reference memos validated and prepared as resident tiles with their tail, teardown
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_workspace_score.f90` — the polar workspace's scoring: block validation, the per-tile graph, the draw, copy-out
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_workspace_shiftmap.f90` — the polar workspace's shift maps: the particle-reusing contraction, the direction transform and requested posterior outputs
        - `mlxf_toy_polarft_workspace_tail.f90` — the polar workspace's fused tail: a Metal kernel per tile for the distances and the posterior draw of every pair
      - **projector/** — the projector toy: projector with its GPU workspace and the batch projector, and their tester
        - `mlxf_toy_projector.f90` — the toy projector (test only): a miniature of SIMPLE's projector with the image procedures the reprojection calls
        - `mlxf_toy_projector_mlx.f90` — the toy projector on MLX (glue): its device state, the padded transform, the expanded cube and the gather's settings
        - `mlxf_toy_projector_pft_batch.f90` — the toy batch projector (test only): SIMPLE's fproject_polar_batch_opt, the projection of a state's reference bank
        - `mlxf_toy_projector_pft_batch_mlx.f90` — the toy batch projector on MLX (glue): the gather through the projector's workspace, to the host or left on the device
        - `mlxf_toy_projector_tester.f90` — tests of the toy projector: the polar gather against the host oracle, its controls, repeatability, its lifecycle
        - `mlxf_toy_projector_workspace.f90` — the toy projector's GPU workspace (test only): the padded transform, the expanded cube and the polar gather in two forms
      - **recon/** — the reconstruction toy: reconstructor_pcg with its GPU workspace, the PCG engine's record and its device engine, and their testers
        - `mlxf_toy_pcg_solver.f90` — the toy PCG engine's record (test only): SIMPLE's pcg_solver_outcome of simple_pcg_solver, with its kill
        - `mlxf_toy_pcg_solver_mlx.f90` — the toy PCG engine on MLX (test only): SIMPLE's abstract operator and pcg_solve of simple_pcg_solver on device vectors with host scalars
        - `mlxf_toy_pcg_solver_tester.f90` — tests of the toy PCG engine: its stops on constructed systems, and the stencil problem against host Cholesky
        - `mlxf_toy_reconstructor_pcg.f90` — the toy reconstructor_pcg (test only): a miniature of SIMPLE's PCG reconstruction from the raw accumulators to the map
        - `mlxf_toy_reconstructor_pcg_mlx.f90` — the toy reconstructor_pcg on MLX (glue): its device state, the device forms of the operator, the engine's adapter and the transfers
        - `mlxf_toy_reconstructor_pcg_tester.f90` — tests of the toy reconstructor_pcg: the operator, preconditioner, kernel and right-hand side against the host oracle
        - `mlxf_toy_reconstructor_pcg_tester_solve.f90` — the toy reconstructor_pcg's solve gates: iterates against the oracle under rules E, F2, F5 and T, start and ship, repeatability
        - `mlxf_toy_reconstructor_pcg_workspace.f90` — the toy reconstructor_pcg's device state (test only): the kernel and preconditioner spectra, envelopes, mask, right-hand side
      - `mlxf_toy_device_work.f90` — the opaque device state of a toy class (test only): an abstract type with one deferred binding, kill
      - `mlxf_toy_seam_tester.f90` — tests of the toys' seam: the opaque device state's lifecycle on a test double, each class's backends, refusals and cycles
- **test/** — mlxf_test_exec, the one test executable, and the CTest entries
  - **consumer/** — outside-project programs of the installed mlxf module: the consumer check, the public-API list and the examples the documents show
    - `mlxf_api_names.f90` — imports every public name of mlxf; generated by scripts/list_public_api.py, never edited
    - `mlxf_consumer.f90` — outside install consumer: public array transfers, matrix product and exact handle teardown
    - `mlxf_example_differences.f90` — the dtype-and-result table of doc/quickstart.md: one block per row, each asserting its row and printing D<n>: ok
    - `mlxf_example_errors.f90` — failures and ownership a caller handles: a status with mlx_last_error(), the named owner of mlx_view, the session's devices
    - `mlxf_example_first.f90` — the README's first program: two arrays, exp(-matmul(a, b)) on MLX's default device, copied back with a status
  - **offstate/** — the off-state build of the toys: a project of its own that compiles their host files and glue stubs without USE_MLX and without the library, and its program
    - `mlxf_offstate_exec.f90` — the off-state program of the toys: what a build without MLX runs, built without USE_MLX and without the library
  - `mlxf_test_exec.f90` — the one test executable: mlxf_test_exec test=<unit_area|list> [suite=] [device=], expect_abort(s), guard=
- **scripts/** — the static gate and its checks, the formatters, the build and gate helpers, the generator of the bind(c) layer and its prototype list, the install, embed, off-state and release checks
  - **probes/** — C programs that probe MLX behaviour and accuracy through mlx-c, run by hand; their findings are recorded where the wrappers depend on them
